title: THE EFFECTS OF CORRELATED COLOR TEMPERATURE ON SUSTAINED ATTENTION AND MOOD OF UNIVERSITY STUDENTS IN LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS
research_question: 1. Is there a significant effect of correlated color temperature of lighting on sustained attention levels of university students’ in terms of the concentration performance (CP) in d2 Test of Attention? 2. Is there a significant effect of correlated color temperature of lighting on sustained attention levels of university students’ in terms of the number of errors in d2 Test of Attention? 3. Is there a significant effect of correlated color temperature of lighting on university students’ mood?

participants.description: Undergraduate students from Interior Architecture and Environmental Design Department at Bilkent University, Ankara, Turkey. Ages ranged from 18 to 27 (mean age 22.1). The sample included 78 female (80.4%) and 19 male (19.6%) students. One student with dyslexia was excluded.
participants.recruitment: Students from IAED 244 Lighting Design (2014-2015 Spring Semester) and IAED 342 Sustainable Design for Interiors (2014-2015 Spring Semester) courses were chosen due to similar scientific content and lecture hours.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Two identical regular lecture classrooms (5.50 m x 10.94 m x 3.65 m) at Bilkent University. Daylight penetration was totally blocked. Existing lighting was replaced with Philips Master TL-D Super 80 36W/840 1SL for 4000 K (Cool White) and Philips Master TL-D Super 80 36W/865 1SL for 6500 K (Cool Daylight). Both CCTs had a CRI of 85 Ra8 and luminous flux of 3250 Lm (4000K) and 3350 Lm (6500K). Average illuminance was 401 lux for 4000 K and 412 lux for 6500 K at 0.7 meters above floor level. Ceiling and walls were white, flooring dark grey granite tile.

measures.construct: Sustained Attention: Total Number of Items Processed (TN)

findings.antecedent: Correlated Color Temperature (4000 K vs 6500 K)
findings.consequent: Total Number of Items Processed (d2 Test of Attention)
findings.quote: Mann- Whitney U Test indicated that, the effect of CCT on the total number of items processed was not to be significant (U (n1= 44, n2= 53) = 1050, two- tailed, p= 0.402)

findings.antecedent: Correlated Color Temperature (4000 K vs 6500 K)
findings.consequent: Errors of Omission (d2 Test of Attention)
findings.quote: Mann- Whitney U Test indicated that the effect of CCT on the errors of omission was not to be significant (U (n1= 44, n2= 53) = 921, two- tailed, p= 0.075)

findings.antecedent: Correlated Color Temperature (4000 K vs 6500 K)
findings.consequent: Errors of Commission (d2 Test of Attention)
findings.mechanism: 6500 K enhances students’ sustained attention than 4000 K and helps them to become more attentive for not to make mistakes.
findings.quote: Mann- Whitney U Test indicated that the effect of CCT on errors of commission was significant (U (n1= 44, n2= 53) = 723, two- tailed, p= 0.001)

findings.antecedent: Correlated Color Temperature (4000 K vs 6500 K)
findings.mechanism: 6500 K enhances students’ sustained attention than 4000 K.
findings.quote: Mann- Whitney U Test indicated that the effect of CCT on the error percentage was significant (U (n1= 44, n2= 53) = 697, two- tailed p= 0.0001)

findings.antecedent: Correlated Color Temperature (4000 K vs 6500 K)
findings.quote: Mann- Whitney U Test indicated that the effect of CCT on the concentration performance was not to be significant (U (n1= 44, n2= 53) = 1022, two- tailed p= 0.296)
Wilcoxon Sign Test indicated that there were no significant difference between before PA and after PA values (Z (n= 44) = -1.4, two- tailed, p= 0.161)
Wilcoxon Sign Test indicated that there were no significant difference between before NA and after NA values (Z (n= 44) = -0.6, two- tailed, p= 0.547)

findings.mechanism: The expected results were having higher After PA values however according to results After PA values decreased. This result could be caused by several reasons such as the inequal numbers of male and female subjects participated in the experiment because genders might reacted differently to CCT of light.
findings.quote: Wilcoxon Sign Test indicated that there was a significant difference between before PA and after PA values (Z (n= 53) = -2.1, two- tailed, p= 0.034)

findings.mechanism: Having lower After NA value is the desired condition to be calm and concentrated which was the acquired result in 6500 K
findings.quote: Wilcoxon Sign Test indicated that there was a significant difference between before NA and after NA values (Z (n= 53) = -2.9, two- tailed, p= 0.003)

findings.antecedent: PANAS values (Positive Affect, Negative Affect) under 4000 K CCT
findings.consequent: d2 Test of Attention values (TN, EO, EC, E%, CP) under 4000 K CCT
findings.mechanism: The findings of this study did not find any significant relationship between them.
findings.quote: According to the results of Spearman’s Correlation test, there was no significant relationship between PANAS values and d2 Test of Attention values of 4000 K

findings.antecedent: PANAS values (Positive Affect, Negative Affect) under 6500 K CCT
findings.consequent: d2 Test of Attention values (TN, EO, EC, E%, CP) under 6500 K CCT
findings.mechanism: The findings of this study did not find any significant relationship between them.
findings.quote: According to the results of Spearman’s Correlation test, there was no significant relationship between PANAS values and d2 Test of Attention values of 6500 K

mechanisms: The 'model of artificial biotope and organism' (Knez, 1995) suggests that physical variables of the environment, such as lighting, influence individuals’ mood and cognition, and mood has a direct impact on cognition.
6500 K CCT enhances students’ sustained attention by helping them to become more attentive and make fewer mistakes.
Lower Negative Affect (NA) values are a desired condition for calmness and concentration.
moderators: Gender (postulated as a potential moderator for mood effects of CCT, but not formally tested in this study due to unequal distribution).
implementation_implications: The usage of 6500 K CCT is recommended in learning environments to enhance students’ sustained attention.
Fluorescent lighting and/or LED lighting of 6500 K CCT are recommended for learning environments.
Findings are useful for interior architects, environmental psychologists, and educationists interested in school environments, learning, mood, and sustained attention.

limitations: The experiments were conducted in real learning environments with daylight control, but the only limitation for this study is the gender of the subjects due to unequal numbers of male and female students.
Limited age range of participants (18-25 years old).
Limited range of correlated color temperature levels examined (only 4000 K and 6500 K).
Specific type of lighting equipment used (fluorescent lamps) rather than other types like LED lighting.
Experiment sessions were relatively short (10-15 minutes), which might not allow subjects' mood to stabilize or might deteriorate sustained attention over longer periods.

instruments_used.name: d2 Test of Attention
instruments_used.description: Psychometric test measuring attention and concentration performance

instruments_used.name: Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS)
instruments_used.description: 20-item self-report questionnaire assessing current mood states

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Higher Correlated Color Temperature (CCT) light, particularly with increased blue light content, can enhance alertness and improve mood through non-visual pathways.

mechanism_chain.description: Higher CCT light activates intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs), leading to physiological changes that impact alertness and mood, subsequently affecting sustained attention.

steps.to_construct: Activation of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs)
